sentences.text: It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and no prima-facie case is made out against them.
The allegations of dowry demand and harassment of victim/deceased made against applicants are wholly false.
The marriage of deceased with applicant no.1 has taken place on 19.11.2018.

It was the second marriage of the deceased and earlier she was married with one Alok Kumar and she has lodged a first information report against her first husband and his family members on 26.06.2014.
At the time of incident, the deceased was residing at her parental home.
Learned counsel has referred first information report and other documents and submitted that deceased along with her minor daughter has sustained injuries in train accident.

It was submitted that no prima-facie case is made out against the applicants and thus, impugned proceedings are liable to be quashed.
4.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the application and submitted that in view of allegations made in the First Information Report and material collected during investigation, a prima-facie case is made out against applicants.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, FIR or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement reported in AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal, Supreme Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.

sentences.text: It has been held that if a prima facie case is made out disclosing ingredients of the offence, court should not quash the charge sheet/complaint.
It is equally well settled that at this stage questions of fact cannot be examined and a mini trial cannot be held.
7. In the instant matter, perusal of record shows that marriage of deceased with applicant no.1 has taken place on 19.11.2018.
It was alleged that after her marriage, she was continuously harassed by the applicants and co-accused persons.
Applicant no.2 is mother-in-law of deceased.
There are specific allegations against both of the applicants.

It was alleged that on 25.10.2019 the deceased has given birth to a daughter but the applicants continued to harass her and they used to demand an Alto car and ultimately she was turned out from her matrimonial home.

The informant has further alleged that when the applicant no.1 has sent a notice for divorce, the deceased committed suicide at railway track and in the said incident her minor daughter has also sustained injuries.
The informant has made clear allegations that his daughter (deceased) was continuously harassed by the applicants-accused on account of dowry and she has committed suicide due to that reason.

In view of allegations made in the First Information Report and material collected during investigation, it Mohit Rana And Another vs State Of U.P And 2 Others on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161271616/
2 can not be said that no prima-facie case is made out against applicants.

sentences.text: The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicants call for determination on questions of fact, which may adequately be discerned/adjudicated only by the trial court.
Even the submissions made on point of law can also be more appropriately gone into by the trial court.
Considering entire facts, no case for quashing of impugned proceedings is made out against the applicants.
Hence, the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is liable to be dismissed.
8. The instant application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is hereby dismissed.
